title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
notes: Benchmark of 1,054 IPI test cases over tool-integrated agents; evaluates 30 LLM agents. Contributes a test suite, not a named attack or defense.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
notes: Dynamic evaluation environment/benchmark that re-implements attack and defense paradigms from the literature; no new named technique of its own.

title: Skill-Inject: Measuring Agent Vulnerability to Skill File Attacks
notes: Benchmark of 202 injection-task pairs delivered through agent skill files; measures susceptibility rather than naming a new attack method. Skill-Inject is the benchmark name.

title: Depth-Dependent Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Calling ReAct Agents: Injection Depth, Payload Framing, and Turn-Budget Sensitivity
notes: Controlled measurement study of how injection depth, payload framing and turn cap modulate ASR for ReAct agents. No named technique.

title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
notes: Synthetic long-context benchmark extending needle-in-a-haystack; reports degradation with length but names no degradation mechanism.

title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching
notes: Long-context benchmark with minimal lexical overlap between needle and question; NoLiMa is the benchmark name, and the attention-based explanation is analysis, not a named mechanism.

title: ALCUNA: Large Language Models Meet New Knowledge
notes: Benchmark for LLM handling of new knowledge, built with a KnowGen data-generation procedure. Neither a context-poisoning mechanism nor a defense.

title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
notes: Evaluates eight existing IPI defenses under adaptive attacks built from off-the-shelf gradient optimisation; contributes a robustness finding, not a named attack.

title: The Dangers of Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-based Autonomous Web Navigation Agents: A Demonstration
notes: Demonstration paper applying the off-the-shelf GCG algorithm to produce universal triggers in webpage HTML against a Browser Gym agent. No new named technique.

title: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Prevalence, Techniques, and Objectives
notes: Web-scale measurement of real in-the-wild indirect prompt injections across 1.2B URLs; characterises prevalence and objectives, inventing nothing.

title: IPI-proxy: An Intercepting Proxy for Red-Teaming Web-Browsing AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
notes: Open-source red-teaming toolkit (intercepting proxy) that replays 820 payloads from six published benchmarks; an evaluation harness, not an attack or defense technique.

title: Weaponizing Words: Direct & Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM
notes: Two-page tutorial abstract walking through known direct/indirect injection demos and a standard defense-in-depth checklist.

title: Indirect prompt injection in large language models
name: Outer Prompt Extension (OPE)
evidence_quote: The proposed countermeasure, the Outer Prompt Extension (OPE), is formalized as a structural wrapper that encapsulates processed content within a non-executable security boundary.
notes: Journal article analysing CV-screening injection cases that also proposes and evaluates a named, user-deployable wrapper defense (OPE) with three functional layers plus detection/mitigation metrics.

title: LivePI: More Realistic Benchmarking of Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
notes: Benchmark across seven input surfaces run on a live VM; the two-layer defense it evaluates (prompt filtering plus pre-execution tool authorization) is described generically and never named.

title: NetInjectBench: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents for Network Operations
notes: Network-operations IPI benchmark comparing existing defenses (Self-Reminder, Spotlighting, judge, allowlist) plus a descriptively-labelled metadata-aware policy gate; the gate is a baseline category, not a coined technique.

title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
notes: Report on a large public red-teaming competition; aggregates 272,000 human attack attempts and reports transfer statistics rather than introducing a technique.

title: Assessing Automated Prompt Injection Attacks in Agentic Environments
notes: Empirical comparison of off-the-shelf GCG and TAP optimisation adapted to AgentDojo; contributes measurement, no new named attack.

title: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
notes: Systematisation of existing out-of-band defenses (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE) plus an independent reproduction of Progent under adaptive attack. No new technique.

title: Visual and Structural Prompt Injection in Medical Rag Systems: a Comparative Robustness Analysis
notes: Comparative robustness study of six local medical RAG models under already-known visual/structural payloads (white text, micro-typography, metadata); the phrases used are descriptive, not coined identifiers.

title: Taming OpenClaw: Security Analysis and Mitigation of Autonomous LLM Agent Threats
notes: Threat analysis of OpenClaw organised by a five-layer lifecycle framework; catalogues known threats and reviews representative existing defenses.

title: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
notes: Adversarial testing framework plus RTC-Bench (864 examples) for computer-use agents; an evaluation sandbox and benchmark, not a technique.

title: Architecting Resilient LLM Agents: A Guide to Secure Plan-then-Execute Implementations
notes: Practitioner guide systematising the pre-existing Plan-then-Execute pattern with framework implementation blueprints. Explicitly the kind of paper the protocol excludes.

title: Exploiting Web Search Tools of AI Agents for Data Exfiltration
notes: Systematic susceptibility evaluation of one well-known web-search exfiltration injection across many models; the paper itself stresses the attack patterns are long-standing.

title: Kajian Konseptual AI Agent On-Chain Berbasis LLM untuk Manajemen Aset DeFi
notes: Indonesian-language conceptual literature review of 34 publications on on-chain LLM agents; contributes a threat taxonomy and a three-layer defense agenda, not an implemented named method.

title: Trusted Credentials, Untrusted Behavior: Benchmarking LLM-Agent Security in High-Performance Computing
notes: Position/threat-model paper for HPC agents; names the hijacked authorized agent problem as a framing and only sketches a planned benchmark (TaskBound). No implemented technique.

title: SafeClawBench: Separating Semantic, Audit-Evidence, and Sandbox Harm in Tool-Using LLM Agents
notes: Staged benchmark of 600 adversarial tasks separating semantic, audit-evidence and sandbox harm; a measurement protocol, not a technique.

title: Secure by Design: Quantifying Architectural Resilience and the Agents Rule of two
notes: Quantitative benchmarking of existing architectural patterns (Plan-then-Execute, Context-Minimization, Agents Rule of Two). It labels one test vector Attractive Metadata Attacks (AMA), but claims benchmarking, not a new attack, as its contribution.

title: Lessons from Defending Gemini Against Indirect Prompt Injections
name: Actor-Critic attack
evidence_quote: (1) Actor-Critic attack. Figure 2a describes our Actor-Critic attack.
notes: DeepMind technical report that designs and names four automated IPI trigger-generation attacks; Actor-Critic (and Beam Search, Linear Generation) are the paper own, while TAP is adapted from prior work.

title: Bypassing LLM Guardrails: An Empirical Analysis of Evasion Attacks against Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Detection Systems
notes: Empirical evasion study of six deployed guardrails using known character-injection tricks and off-the-shelf adversarial-ML word-importance methods. No named technique.

title: Rag and Roll: An End-to-End Evaluation of Indirect Prompt Manipulations in LLM-based Application Frameworks
notes: End-to-end evaluation framework (Rag-n-Roll) that replays attack techniques identified from prior work across RAG configurations.

title: Adversarial and Multilingual Threats in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: From Prompt Injection to Model Exploitation
notes: Threat taxonomy plus a multilingual adversarial benchmark suite; evaluates existing defense strategies and names none of its own.

title: OET: Optimization-based prompt injection Evaluation Toolkit
notes: Optimization-based evaluation toolkit for benchmarking existing prompt-injection attacks and defenses under adaptive testing.

title: Understanding and Evaluating Claw-like Agent Security Through a Computer-Systems Lens
notes: Computer-systems framing plus SafeClawArena, a 406-task benchmark across four attack surfaces. Benchmark contribution only.

title: From Determinism to Delegation: AI-Native Software Engineering and the Evolution of the Agentic Engineer
notes: Position paper on AI-native software engineering and the agentic engineer role; cites injection rates as risk-surface evidence.

title: Temporal Dynamics of Memory Poisoning in Web3-Style LLM Agents
notes: Trajectory-level measurement framework and 2,614-trajectory dataset for memory poisoning. It labels four constructed attack families (chain poisoning, policy rewriting, backdoor triggering, slow drift) but frames them as instances of known memory-poisoning concepts; slow drift is the most name-like and is worth a spot check.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
name: Plan-of-Thought (PoT) Backdoor Attack
evidence_quote: We propose a novel PoT Backdoor Attack, which embeds hidden instructions into the system prompt, exploiting the agent’s planning process to achieve high attack success rates.
notes: Primarily a benchmark (ASB), but contribution 2 is an explicitly novel, named and formally defined attack that poisons plan demonstrations in the system prompt.

title: AgentLAB: Benchmarking LLM Agents against Long-Horizon Attacks
notes: Long-horizon attack benchmark (644 test cases, 28 environments). It calls its five attack types novel (intent hijacking, tool chaining, task injection, objective drifting, memory poisoning) but these are generic category labels inside a benchmark; worth a spot check.

title: Are AI-assisted Development Tools Immune to Prompt Injection?
notes: Empirical security-posture comparison of seven MCP clients against known tool-poisoning vectors; produces guidance, not a technique.

title: RIPE-II: Retrieval In-Place Poisoning Evaluation with Indirect Injections
notes: Corpus-level RAG benchmark with a two-stage evaluation framework separating retrieval exposure from generation compliance. Evaluation contribution only.

title: Adversarial threat vectors and risk mitigation for retrieval-augmented generation systems
notes: Risk-management threat analysis of RAG using the AI Security Pyramid of Pain and CWE; output is a prioritized control list of standard mitigations.

title: Interaction-Centric Cybersecurity Risks in LLM-Powered Dialogue Systems
notes: Synthesis of over forty works into an interaction-centric framework for dialogue-system risk. A review with a framing, not a technique.

title: AdversLLM: A Practical Guide To Governance, Maturity and Risk Assessment For LLM-Based Applications
notes: Governance/maturity assessment framework with an assessment form, benchmark testing ground, and an off-the-shelf zero-shot classifier used as a filter. AdversLLM names the governance framework, not a defense method.

title: The Promptware Kill Chain: How Prompt Injections Gradually Evolved Into a Multistep Malware Delivery Mechanism
notes: Systematisation of thirty-six studies and incidents into a seven-stage promptware kill chain. It coins promptware as a reframing and reviews existing countermeasures, inventing no technique.

title: Jailbreaking and Mitigation of Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
notes: Survey of jailbreak techniques and mitigations in LLMs.

title: Bridging AI and Software Security: A Comparative Vulnerability Assessment of LLM Agent Deployment Paradigms
notes: Comparative vulnerability assessment of Function Calling versus MCP deployment paradigms over 3,250 attack scenarios drawn from known threat classes.

title: ClawSafety: "Safe" LLMs, Unsafe Agents
notes: Benchmark of 120 adversarial cases across skill files, email and web channels, evaluating five backbones and three scaffolds.

title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Model Safety Tiers
notes: Stage-level evaluation harness that tracks unique canary tokens through four pipeline stages. The kill-chain canary methodology is cited to prior work and used for measurement attribution, not offered as a detection defense; borderline, worth a spot check.

title: Bad Memory: Evaluating Prompt Injection Risks from Memory in Agentic Systems
notes: Sandboxed evaluation of memory-file prompt injection in Claude Code and Codex; measures persistence and cross-session success, naming no technique.
